capabilities: Track local AI agent sessions by project and status
Delegate a task line to a chosen agent and model
Write progress, duration, tokens and conclusions back into journal notes
Show token heatmaps and per-agent, per-project usage dashboards
Distil long-term memories from journals and inject them into delegations
extras: Desktop only (Obsidian 1.4.0+, mobile unsupported); the macOS menu bar is macOS-specific; the full compatibility matrix and per-client requirements are in an external Wiki; Apache 2.0.
motivation: The author's stated stage-one goal is to make notes, daily journals, project tasks and distilled memories an effective, low-noise, traceable context provider for every connected agent.
problem: AI agent sessions run in separate terminals and apps, so their status, token use and results are not visible or recorded next to the notes that prompted them.

relations.evidence: pair it with Nautilus Spiral so Agent Deck owns the AI writes while Spiral keeps its schedule and progress display
task keywords such as DOING / PAUSED / TOREVIEW / DONE are coloured and iconified in both editing and reading views, matching Logseq Style Tasks

requires.name: Local AI agent clients (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, etc.)

summary: Control deck that tracks local AI agent sessions, delegates tasks from notes, and writes progress and results back as Markdown.
